dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Haha! Explosives! My kind of fun!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you suddenly so excited? We don't even know how powerful these explosives are! What if we hurt innocent bystanders?

choices.text: Blasting fish is blasting fish, just toss 'em into the lake.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But when you put it like that... Paimon really does want to try...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Normally we're always hearing about how Klee wants to blast fish, is blasting fish, or is getting punished for doing it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now that Paimon is here, by the lakeside, with a box of explosives beside her... Paimon really wants to try it, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Throwing just one should be... no big deal, right?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Together with Paimon, you open the suspicious wooden box and each take out a bomb. After studying how to ignite the fuses, both of you count down "3, 2, 1" and set the detonators, and both of you throw the bombs far into Cider Lake...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: A low rumble comes from underwater, and two giant spouts of water explode from the surface of the lake, sending a few Anglers spinning high into the sky...\nYou and Paimon give each other a high-five with big smiles on your faces, and get ready to high-tail it out of there...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: But "Operation Impulsively Secretly Blast Fish" did not go as swimmingly as it appeared. Almost as soon as the bombs exploded, you were exposed...

response.speaker: Distant Scream
response.text: Aaaaaaahhhhh!

response.speaker: Distant Scream
response.text: My ears!!!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: That scared me half to death! How are you, Phonia, are you okay?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: A sudden underwater explosion... It almost deafened me! Judging by the sonic signature of that explosion... It must have been one of your bombs, Ematol!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Ha? Really? Have I not been standing obendiently by your side this whole time, doing nothing? Do I look like I have bombs in my hands?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: You! You must've set timed bombs into the lake beforehand, just to see me in this awful state!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: If that were true, then shouldn't I also have set up Kameras to capture the sight of you holding your head crying on the ground like a baby? Would be a great shame not to have such photos for posterity!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: You! Don't expect any discount from me for your next month's rent! And the water bill, furniture, and all that food you mooched... I let it all slide before, but now it's time to pay up!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Wait, wait, wait, no, no! I shouldn't have laughed! Phonia, my dearest sister, even if I was responsible for the last few dozen pranks... It really wasn't me this time! I swear!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: If I really could make... timed detonators that were extremely reliable despite staying submerged for a long time...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: We wouldn't have needed to risk our lives to manually detonate the bombs when we ambushed the Hilichurls last time, would we?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: ...Right. You're too simple-minded to use timed fuses to pull a prank on me.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: You!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: You tricked me, too! Didn't you say that any loud noises would damage your hearing while you're using that detection equipment?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Since you seem to have no difficulties arguing, you don't seem to have gone deaf!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: You don't get it! Hearing damage is accumulative and only manifests in stages! By shouting and talking back at me so loudly right now, you're increasing the damage!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Maybe one day, I won't be able to distinguish the signature patterns of soundwaves anymore! And then I'd lose my job!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: And then, you won't have a place to stay either, because I would have to rent the whole house to someone who can afford higher rent! And then... then ... I'll become a fisherwoman! Anyway, I won't take of you, that's for sure!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Then... Then I'll argue with you more quietly... I'll keep it quiet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't make out what they're saying... All they care about is arguing with each other.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It was really fun! Maybe if we just toss one more...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no! Once was enough. If we throw any more, those two will definitely come to investigate. We can't get caught!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Though it feels like we caused... a mess, but not an overly large one, at least Paimon's curiosity has been completely satisfied!

choices.text: Now, give it all you've got!
Don't you want to know what it's like to chuck some bombs?

dialogues.speaker: Suspicious Wooden Chest
dialogues.text: A suspicious wooden box, never seen before. A piece of paper is lodged in the cracks between the boards on the lid. Written on it is "Property of the Investigation Team. Materials of the highest grade of danger are within. Handle with care."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That note on the box sounds... terrifying!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why would something so obviously dangerous be left right by Cider Lake? Could it belong to those two knights over there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like there's a wide gap between the planks! We should be able to see inside!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon have a look... It appears to be filled with... lots of round, red objects, much larger than Sunsettias...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why would the Knights of Favonius leave a box of explosives by the lake? Are they planning to blow up... those invasive fish that Lisa mentioned?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Whoa! So scary! Let's get out of here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right! A whole box of bombs! We should get as far away from something that dangerous as we can!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Whoa! It's so scary! Let's run!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even you think it's dangerous!? Does that mean that this box is oozing murderous intent... Let's get out of here!
